Hi Jillian — thanks for the quick review and the clear asks. High-level answers below and I'm attaching a short evidence package (runbook excerpt, RTO/RPO matrix, and an architecture diagram).

- RTO / RPO: Our production design targets an RTO of 2 hours and an RPO of 15 minutes for primary stateful services (managed PostgreSQL clusters and Redis KV). For lower-tier services we have RTOs up to 24 hours and RPO up to 1 hour depending on the workload. Please see attached rto_rpo_matrix.csv for per-service SLAs and the runbook excerpt that documents the restoration steps we exercise in our quarterly DR test.

- Cross-region failover: We operate a warm-standby architecture across two regions (us-west-2 primary, us-east-1 secondary). The failover process is executed via our orchestrated playbook: snapshot promotion of read-replicas, automated DNS cutover, and KV cache warm-up steps to reduce cold-start impact. The attached aws-regions-failover-diagram.png illustrates the flow.

- Backups and retention: Full daily snapshots retained for 30 days, incremental snapshots retained for 7 days, and point-in-time backups enabled for 7 days on primary DB (we can extend per-contract). Restoration SLA for customer-impacting incidents is within the RTO above; non-customer-impacting restores (ad-hoc) are typically completed within 8 business hours.

I'm looping in Vivek (infra) and Marissa (customer success) to confirm a couple technical items and to coordinate delivery of the final evidence bundle. If a short call helps, I can schedule one Friday morning.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Head of Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

Laura / Marissa — answers below from the infra runbook and our most recent drill (2027-04-09):

- DB full-restore time (tested): 1 hour 45 minutes from snapshot-to-promoted-primary for our standard 3-node managed Postgres clusters (this matches the RTO column in rto_rpo_matrix.csv). We document the test steps and timestamps in the runbook (attached excerpt) and the drill artifacts are in JIRA SEC-6632.

- Warm-standby readiness: Secondary is maintained as an automated read-replica, but promotion relies on an orchestrated process that includes a short manual approval step (safety hold) — the orchestration completes in ~10 minutes after approval, cache warm-up and DNS cutover add ~20–30 minutes depending on DNS TTLs. In practice the full failover window we measured in the drill was ~35–55 minutes depending on smoke-test remediation.

- Additional artifacts: I'm attaching a 2-page runbook excerpt showing the promotion commands, TTL recommendations (30s for critical endpoints during failover), and the smoke-test checklist we run post-cutover. Backup retention policy: daily full for 30 days, incremental for 7 days; archived monthly snapshots retained for 1 year for compliance customers.

If MediTrust needs shorter RTO/RPO we can propose a dedicated DR posture (active-active or synchronous cross-region replication) as an add-on; happy to draft numbers.

—Vivek
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
